transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?
I came in because I barely want to eat anymore. At work on my lunch break, I’ll look at food I used to like, but I just don’t want it. I end up throwing most of it away.
Are you worried about gaining weight or becoming fat?
No, I haven’t really been worried about my weight. It’s not that—I just don’t feel like eating.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or sad lately?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed feeling especially sad or depressed.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in doing things you normally enjoy?

Yeah. I used to look forward to gallery nights, playing basketball, even getting tacos from food trucks or helping kids with art projects. Lately I just feel flat when I’m there, and usually make an excuse to leave.
How long have you been feeling this way?
About two months, I think. It started after I got that window display award and the district manager gave me all that attention.
How has your sleep been lately?
Most nights I just lie there replaying the award thing and conversations at the store. And when I do get to sleep, I wake up really early and can’t get my mind to shut off again.
Have you been having feelings of guilt or feeling down on yourself recently?

Yeah. I keep thinking I didn’t deserve that award, or even the chance to be a supervisor. It feels like I fooled everybody somehow, even though people keep telling me I earned it. I feel guilty about it.
With everything you've been feeling, have you had any thoughts of death, or thoughts of harming yourself?
No, I haven’t had thoughts about dying or doing anything to hurt myself.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or lacking energy during this time?
Yeah. By the middle of a shift, my body feels heavy. Even straightening racks or walking back to the stockroom takes more out of me than it feels like it should.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating, focusing, or making everyday decisions?
Yeah. At work I keep losing my place on simple things, like counting inventory. Even picking colors for a display, I second-guess myself over stuff I used to do quickly.
